spot.name: Kissimmee Prairie Preserve
spot.notes: Florida's first DarkSky park. The gate closes 15 minutes after sunset, so reserve a campsite or astronomy pad and check in with the ranger before dark; red lights only on the pads.

spot.name: Salt Springs Recreation Area
spot.notes: The largest campground in the Ocala National Forest, and the only one with full RV hookups. Gates close in the evening (8 PM in summer), so check in early; there's no cell service.

spot.name: Withlacoochee River Park
spot.notes: The St. Petersburg Astronomy Club's dark-sky site: astronomers camp on the open activity field on new-moon weekends, since the campground is shaded by oaks. The park is open dawn to dusk, so stay with a campsite.

spot.name: Alexander Springs Recreation Area
spot.notes: Forest Service campground beside the spring. Campers get 24-hour gate access with a code; day-use hours vary by season.

spot.name: Clearwater Lake Campground
spot.notes: 42-site Forest Service campground with lakefront sites. Campers get 24-hour gate access with a code; day use ends at 4 PM.

spot.name: Lake Griffin State Park
spot.notes: Campers only after dark: the park closes at sundown, and campers arriving after sunset must call before 5 PM for the gate combination.

spot.name: Little Manatee River State Park
spot.notes: Campers only after dark: the park closes at sundown, and campers arriving after sunset must call before 5 PM for the gate combination.

spot.name: Manatee Hammock Campground
spot.notes: County campground on the Indian River facing the Kennedy Space Center launch pads. The park is open dawn to dusk, and anyone who isn't a registered camper must leave by 10 PM.

spot.name: Sebastian Inlet State Park
spot.notes: Open 24 hours with a staffed north ranger station, so no campsite is needed. Use the north-side lots; south-side beach access is closed during bridge construction.

spot.name: Hopkins Prairie
spot.notes: Small Forest Service campground overlooking an open prairie, with vault toilets and no electricity. Come in from SR 19 via FR 86 and FR 111, since Google Maps' northern route doesn't work.

spot.name: Moss Park
spot.notes: County campground between Lake Hart and Lake Mary Jane. The park closes at 6 PM in winter and 8 PM in summer, so after dark it's campers only.

spot.name: Wekiwa Springs State Park
spot.notes: Campers only after dark: the park closes at sundown, and campers arriving after sunset call 407-553-4383 for the gate combination. Day visitors need an entry reservation.

spot.name: Trimble Park
spot.notes: Small county campground on a point between Lake Carlton and Lake Beauclair. The park closes at 6 PM in winter and 8 PM in summer, so after dark it's campers only.

spot.name: Daytona Beach at Main Street
spot.notes: The beach is open to pedestrians 24 hours, tides permitting, but cars are allowed only by day, so park off the beach near the Main Street Pier. Keep lights off the sand, which confuse nesting sea turtles.

spot.name: Holder Mine Campground
spot.notes: Improved state forest campground with electric sites, reserved through ReserveAmerica. Busy with hunters during archery and small-game seasons.

spot.name: Three Lakes WMA, Prairie Lakes Unit
spot.seasonalNote: No camping during Prairie Lakes quota hunts
spot.notes: Primitive campsites by Lake Jackson need a free FWC camping permit, plus a daily-use permit to enter. Come in from CR 523 via Prairie Lakes Rd, since the route from SR 60 doesn't go through.

spot.name: Fisheating Creek Campground
spot.notes: Concession-run campground in the Fisheating Creek WMA with RV and primitive sites; camping permits come from Fisheating Creek Outpost. Busiest on weekends and in the cooler months.

spot.name: Juniper Springs Recreation Area
spot.notes: Forest Service campground around the spring. Campers get 24-hour gate access with a code; the boardwalk is closed for renovation.

spot.name: Blue Spring State Park
spot.notes: Campers only after dark: the park closes at sundown, and campers arriving after sunset call 386-775-3663 for the gate combination. A camping reservation doubles as the entry reservation.

spot.name: Lake Louisa State Park
spot.notes: Campers only after dark: the park closes at sundown, and campers arriving late must call 352-394-3969 for the gate code before closing.

spot.name: Hillsborough River State Park
spot.notes: Campers only after dark: the park closes at sundown, and campers arriving after sunset must call before 5 PM for the gate combination.

spot.name: UCF Reflecting Pond
spot.notes: Campus lawn by Millican Hall where UCF's Planetary Sciences Group has set up telescopes for Moon viewing; good for the Moon and planets, not the Milky Way. Visitors need an $8 virtual daily parking permit.

spot.name: Bill Frederick Park at Turkey Lake
spot.notes: City park with RV sites and cabins on Turkey Lake. It closes at 5 PM from November to March and 7 PM from April to October, so after dark it's overnight guests only; best for the Moon and planets.

spot.name: Black Point Wildlife Drive
spot.notes: Wide marsh views over the Indian River, but refuge roads are open sunrise to sunset only, so there is no night access.

spot.name: Colt Creek State Park
spot.notes: Campers only after dark: the park closes at sundown, and campers arriving after sunset must call before 5 PM for the gate combination.

spot.name: Cranes Roost Park
spot.notes: City lakefront park open until 11 PM (midnight on Friday and Saturday). It's brightly lit, so come for the Moon, planets and the brightest stars.

spot.name: Fort De Soto Park Campground
spot.notes: County campground near the mouth of Tampa Bay. The front gate is locked from 9 PM to 5:30 AM, and registered campers get the gate combination at check-in.

spot.name: Jetty Park
spot.notes: The park closes at 9 PM except to campground guests, who keep beach access and 24-hour pier access. Campers can stay overnight to watch launches from the beach or pier.

spot.name: Kelly Park / Rock Springs
spot.notes: County park that closes at 6 PM in winter and 8 PM in summer. After hours the waterfront is closed and campers must stay in the campground.

spot.name: Lake Apopka Wildlife Drive
spot.notes: One-way 11-mile drive open to cars Friday to Sunday and federal holidays. The gate takes vehicles 7 AM to 3 PM and everyone must be out by 5 PM, so there is no night access.

spot.name: Lake Eola Park
spot.notes: City park that stays open until midnight. Good for the Moon, planets and bright satellite passes; the Milky Way is washed out.

spot.name: Lake Kissimmee State Park
spot.seasonalNote: Campgrounds closed for renovation since February 2026
spot.notes: The park closes at sundown, and its campgrounds are closed for renovation with no reopening date, so there is no night access for now.

spot.name: Lighthouse Point Park
spot.notes: County inlet park that closes at 7:30 PM in October and November, 6 PM in winter and 9 PM in summer, always before true darkness, so there is no night access.

spot.name: Playalinda Beach
spot.notes: The seashore is open 6 AM to 6 PM under normal hours and closes for some rocket launches, so there is no night access.

spot.name: Silver Springs State Park
spot.notes: Campers only after dark: the park closes at sundown, and the campground has its own entrance at 1425 NE 58th Ave. Campers arriving after sunset must call before 5 PM for the gate combination.
